column1: # kit-files.tsv — the single record of which files the kit manages, and how.
# Read by BOTH install-kit.sh (which applies them) and bin/kit.mjs (which checks
# them). Neither tool holds its own copy of this list — that is the entire point.
# An installer and a checker that each know the file list will drift apart, and
# Format: four TAB-separated columns, always four, in application order.
# `template` is the file under templates/ to copy from, or `-` when the source
# lives at the same path inside the kit. `-` is required rather than an empty
# field: tab is an IFS whitespace character, so bash collapses consecutive tabs
# and an empty column would shift every field after it.
#   overwrite                 copied from the kit every run; local edits are destroyed
#   seed                      copied only when absent; source is the same path in the kit
#   create-if-absent          copied only when absent; source is templates/<template>
#   create-if-absent-stamped  as above, substituting YYYY-MM-DD and KIT-VERSION
#   overwrite-or-suffix       as overwrite, but yields the filename to a repo that already owns
#                             it, installing the kit copy as <name>-kit.<ext> instead
#   managed-block             rewritten between the KIT:START / KIT:END markers only
# Behaviors handled directly by install-kit.sh and listed here only so the checker
# knows the file is kit-managed: managed-block.
# See docs/kit-distribution.md for what each behavior means for a consumer.
# /semver is a real command consumers benefit from, but the name is already
# taken in repos that built their own release tooling (jwilleke/ngdpbase bumps
# src/utils/version.ts; jwilleke/mjs-ha tags date-stamped snapshots). Those
# repos keep their command and receive the kit's as semver-kit.md.
